notes: The Crisis (Plans 5b and 6, design §10b): each world rolls one villain, favoured where one of its threats holds a land. Each of its three acts is an investigation at its lead site (henchmen; act I's is where the plan is learned), then a prevention at its key site against the act's boss, on a fixed calendar (act n opens on day 100(n − 1) + 30 and is due on day 100n). Boss styles: a finale villain's lieutenants (each act's `boss`) hold acts I and II and the villain is met at act III (the Ashen Prophet, the Pretender's Hand); a recurring villain is met at every key site, stronger each time, and remembers the last meeting (the Drake-Speaker). `surge` marks the acts that raise the world's danger near their due day: an army of the dead or of sellswords on the roads, drakes called to the beacons, a wyrm stirring. The site types are the poiTypes in crisis-sites.json (weight 0, category quest). leadCr and keyCr set the encounters' DCs (rules/challenge.ts crDc). Text slots: {villain} (the rolled name, e.g. "Morvaine, the Ashen Prophet"), {land} (the land of the act's lead site, or of its key site in the thwarted and failed texts), {site} (the site's name) and {seat} (the seat of the key site's domain, only in seat acts' thwarted and failed texts). Act I's open and hurry texts may be logged before the plan is known, so they name no villain. Their situations are in crisis-situations.json, and their personal names in crisis-names.json. Original names and texts, written by Claude.

entries.name: the Ashen Prophet
entries.summary: {villain} means to wake the barrow-kings and set a dead one on a living throne.
entries.omen: Graves have been opened in {land}: dug out neatly, at night, by people with lanterns and ladders who took the bones and left the rings. The priest of the old chapel out that way wrote to his bishop about it. Then his chapel burned.
entries.plan: The ledger is kept in a careful hand. {villain} has been buying the dead: barrows from farmers, bones from sextons, and the names of old kings from scholars who did not ask why. First the old barrow-field is to be opened, and Sister Ilse Marrow, who reads to the dead, is to wake its sleepers. Then, in a hidden ossuary, Father Anselm Crake is to teach the dead to march and to keep step to his bells. Last, {villain} will crown the oldest of the barrow-kings again in the royal crypt beneath a living lord's seat, and every grave in the realm is to kneel to him. The last page is a list of dates.

acts.name: The Opened Graves
acts.goal: open the old barrow-field and wake the kings buried there
acts.clue: Night-diggers who pay in grave silver: {villain}'s people are opening barrows somewhere in {land}.
acts.open: Out in {land} graves are being opened at night, neatly, by people with lanterns and ladders. Whoever is buying the bones is in a hurry. Ask in the towns.
acts.hurry: The night-diggers have nearly reached the oldest barrows. If they are not stopped soon, what sleeps there will be awake before the season turns.
acts.thwarted: The barrows of {site} are shut again, Sister Ilse's reading is over and the woken dead are back in the ground. {villain} will have heard by now.
acts.failed: The barrow-field stands open. What woke there walks out across {land} in a long, quiet line, with Sister Ilse reading it on, and {villain} walks with it.

acts.name: The Bone Choir
acts.goal: teach the risen dead to march as one
acts.clue: Bone-carts that pay in grave silver come and go by night: {villain}'s people are buying the dead in {land}.
acts.open: Covered carts are on the roads of {land} again, heaped and riding low, going somewhere by night. {villain} is gathering the dead for something bigger than a barrow-field.
acts.hurry: The bells ring every night now, and the dead on the roads keep step to them. Father Anselm Crake's choir has nearly learned its song: twenty days, and it marches.
acts.thwarted: The choir of {site} is broken, its bells cracked and Father Anselm silent among them. Without the beat the dead wander and fall, and {villain} has lost an army before it could march.
acts.failed: The choir has learned its song. Father Anselm rings it out of {land}, and an army of the dead marches in step behind him. No wall it comes to stays standing for long.

acts.name: The Ashen Crowning
acts.goal: crown a barrow-king in the crypt beneath a living lord's seat
acts.clue: Pilgrims with ash on their brows are gathering at a hostel in {land}: {villain}'s faithful, on their way to a crowning.
acts.open: Pilgrims with ash on their brows walk the roads of {land}, singing a dead king's name. {villain} has called the faithful to a crowning.
acts.hurry: Frost in the cellars and ash on the crypt steps: the crowning is close. Twenty days, and a dead king opens his eyes.
acts.thwarted: The crown is off the dead king's head and the rite is ash. {villain} falls among the tombs of {site} with nothing left to raise.
acts.failed: Beneath {seat} a dead king opens his eyes with a crown on his head, and every grave in the realm turns towards him. The living have lost the realm.

entries.victory: {villain} is dead and stays dead: you made sure of it. The barrows are shut, the choir is silent and the crypt is sealed. The graves will be quiet for a long time.

entries.name: the Pretender's Hand
entries.summary: {villain}, a disinherited heir, is buying swords and forging proof for a crown.
entries.omen: Couriers keep going missing on the roads of {land}, and the ones who turn up again carry letters nobody sent. The last was found in a ditch with his bag slit open and his seal gone. His camp is still out there, if the crows have left anything.
entries.plan: The dispatches are in cipher, and the cipher is careless. {villain} was cut out of a royal will and means to write a better one. First the old king's seal is to be stolen and copied, and Agathe Wren, the Hand's steward, is to see that a will naming {villain} heir is found in good time. Then a border garrison is to be bought outright, captain and all, with silver the bandit roads have been collecting for a year, and Captain Ulrika Hask of the Grey Company is to hold the muster until it is paid. Last, {villain} is to be crowned in a seat's own chapel, with bought swords at the door and the forged will on the altar, before the true lords can ride. Every order is signed the same way: by the Pretender's Hand.

acts.name: The Stolen Seal
acts.goal: copy the old king's seal onto a forged will
acts.clue: A master forger has dropped off the guild rolls, and his last order was paid in {villain}'s silver: look for him in {land}.
acts.open: Couriers are going missing on the roads of {land}, and letters nobody sent are turning up in their place. Someone is building a lie, one seal at a time. Ask in the towns.
acts.hurry: A will that should not exist is nearly finished. Once it is sealed and found, no court in the realm will be able to unsee it. There is little time.
acts.thwarted: The forged will is ash, the copied seal is broken, Agathe Wren is finished as the Hand's steward and the forger at {site} is talking to anyone who will listen. {villain} will need another proof.
acts.failed: A will turns up in {land}, sealed with the old king's own seal and naming {villain} heir. Agathe Wren carries it from court to court. Half the lords who read it believe it, and the other half are paid to.

acts.name: The Bought Garrison
acts.goal: buy a border garrison with stolen silver
acts.boss: Captain Ulrika Hask of the Grey Company
acts.clue: The bandits of {land} have stopped robbing for themselves: every road's takings go to one counting-house, and from there to {villain}.
acts.open: Bandits on the roads of {land} pay their takings to one counting-house now, and the counting-house pays swords. {villain} is buying an army.
acts.hurry: Sellswords crowd the roads to the muster, and Captain Ulrika Hask has nearly been paid her price. Twenty days, and the garrison opens its gates from the inside.
acts.thwarted: The muster at {site} breaks up. The silver is gone, Captain Hask's company has scattered, and the garrison {villain} paid for will not open its gates.
acts.failed: The garrison has taken {villain}'s silver. Captain Hask opens its gates from the inside, and {villain}'s banner flies over {land}.

acts.name: The False Coronation
acts.goal: be crowned in a seat's own chapel before the true lords can ride
acts.clue: A bishop has gone to his summer house in {land} with a guard of knights and a goldsmith's parcel: {villain} has bought a crowning.
acts.open: A bishop of {land} has left his see with a guard of bought knights, and a goldsmith has been paid for a crown. {villain} means to be crowned within the season.
acts.hurry: The true lords are still arguing over who rides first, and {villain} has stopped arguing. Twenty days, and there will be a crowned king to ride against.
acts.thwarted: The crowning at {site} is broken up, the crown is in the dirt and the bishop has fled. Nobody kneels to {villain} now.
acts.failed: {villain} is crowned at {seat} with bought swords at the door. By the time the true lords ride there is a king to ride against, and a war that will last a generation.

entries.victory: {villain} is taken in chains, still insisting. The forged will is ash, the bought swords have gone home and the crown is back in its vault. The realm keeps its king, for whatever he is worth.

entries.name: the Drake-Speaker
entries.summary: {villain}, an outcast who talks to drakes, means to wake the old wyrm under the mountain.
entries.omen: Drakes are taking the flocks in the hills of {land}, and the shepherds say someone walks with them when they come down to feed. One shepherd's hut, on a hill burned black, took the worst of it. Nobody has heard from him since.
entries.plan: The shepherd heard all of it through the wall. {villain} was driven out of the giant clans for talking to drakes, and the drakes talked back. First a clutch of drake eggs is to be stolen from a brood cave, so that the wyrm's heralds hatch to {villain}'s voice. Then the old beacons on the heights are to be lit: the fires that once called the wyrm down to feed. Last, the wyrm itself is to be woken in the giants' hall under the mountain, where it has slept since before there were kings. {villain} means to be there in person, every time, and believes the wyrm will listen.

acts.name: The Stolen Clutch
acts.goal: steal a drake clutch and hatch the wyrm's heralds
acts.clue: Burned goats and a broken drake egg on the scree: {villain} has been robbing broods in {land}.
acts.open: Drakes are coming down out of the high country of {land} to take the flocks, and the shepherds swear someone walks with them. Ask in the towns.
acts.hurry: Somewhere in the hills a stolen clutch of drake eggs lies warm and nearly ready to hatch, and someone sings to it every night. There is little time.
acts.thwarted: The stolen eggs of {site} are smashed or back under their mother. {villain} got away on drake-back, shouting that this is not over, and has no heralds to raise.
acts.failed: The clutch hatches to {villain}'s voice. A brood of young drakes takes the skies over {land}, and they answer to no one else.

acts.name: The Burning Beacons
acts.goal: light the old watch-fires that once called the wyrm to feed
acts.clue: Giants are felling whole woods in {land} and hauling them off by night: {villain} is gathering fuel for fires.
acts.open: Whole hillsides of trees are coming down in {land}, felled by giants and dragged away by night. {villain} has not forgotten you, and has not stopped.
acts.hurry: Drakes circle the old beacon hills every evening now, waiting to be called, and they hunt the roads while they wait. Twenty days, and {villain} lights the fires.
acts.thwarted: The beacons of {site} are cold and their wood is thrown down the hill. {villain} flew off on Ashmaw's back again, swearing that next time will be the last. Nothing under the mountain heard.
acts.failed: The beacons burn all night across {land}, and something under the mountain hears them and turns over in its sleep.

acts.name: The Waking
acts.goal: wake the old wyrm in the hall under the mountain
acts.clue: The hot springs of {land} have run dry and the ground shakes under them: {villain}'s people are digging down to something.
acts.open: The ground shakes in {land} and the hot springs have run dry. {villain} is looking for the way into the mountain, and the drakes are restless on every road.
acts.hurry: The quakes come every night now, and the drakes no longer come down to feed: they wait. Twenty days, and something under the mountain wakes.
acts.thwarted: The waking is broken off. The wyrm settles back into its sleep, and this time {villain} does not get away: the Speaker lies buried in {site} beside it.
acts.failed: The wyrm wakes. {villain} speaks to it, and for a moment it listens. Then it eats {villain} and goes looking for more, and {land} burns first.

entries.victory: {villain} is dead, the clutch is broken and the beacons are cold. Under the mountain the old wyrm sleeps on, and with luck nobody will be fool enough to try waking it again.
